proof.title: Built for yesterday's climate. Exposed to tomorrow's.
proof.body: Over the past twenty years, economic losses from natural disasters have tripled. Many industrial sites and infrastructure still in operation today were designed for a climate that no longer exists. Shutdowns are multiplying, insurance premiums are climbing, and the question is no longer "should we adapt?" but "how do we prioritize our investments?".

proof.stat3_label: Of industrial sites analyzed have at least one uncovered critical vulnerability
proof.quote_text: So many constants are turning into variables that we urgently need to rethink climate risk management — not as a fix, but as a strategic adaptation capability. The reality is clear: climate is no longer something we observe from a distance, it has become an immediate strategic parameter.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Why isn't an exposure analysis enough?
faq.a1: An exposure analysis tells you that a hazard is coming — heatwaves, floods, drought… — but not whether your roof will fail, at what temperature your control systems shut down, or how many production days you will lose. Translating exposure into a quantified investment decision requires drilling down to the physical and financial vulnerability of each of your sites. Without this, you can neither quantify your real cost of inaction nor prioritize adaptation measures by ROI.
faq.q2: What is the difference between your physical & financial vulnerability analysis and the statistical vulnerability analysis used by the rest of the market?
faq.a2: Statistical vulnerability relies on generic damage functions built on past climate events. The result: a theoretical cost of inaction, a standard list of non-prioritized measures, and no actionable trajectory. Our physical and financial vulnerability uses your specific damage functions — through a digital twin of each site and our R&D — relevant for prospective climate events. You get the real cost of inaction, a resilience score per site and at group level, specific measures prioritized by ROI, and an actionable trajectory you can steer over time.
faq.q3: How do you build the digital twin? Does it take a lot of time from our teams?
faq.a3: Our digital twin is based on 9 systems of an infrastructure: building envelope, people, equipment, stocks, processes, external dependencies, outdoor spaces, governance, prevention. It is built mostly from automated reading of client documents through the platform. The load on your teams therefore stays very light: sharing existing documents and, occasionally during pilots, a few targeted interviews are enough; we take care of the modeling and quantification on our side.
faq.q4: How long before we see results?
faq.a4: We typically start with a year 1 pilot on a number of your critical sites, then roll out to the rest of your portfolio in year 2.

publications.title: Adapting industrial sites to heatwaves
publications.desc: Heatwaves are no longer a cyclical risk but a systemic and growing threat to the industrial sector. Built for yesterday's climate, many production sites are now vulnerable, experiencing production stops, equipment failures, and increased risks to workers' health. This white paper offers methodological directions and action levers to analyze the exposure and vulnerability of an industrial site, simulate the impacts, and deploy an effective and resilient adaptation program.

publications.title: Regeneration in service of business resilience
publications.authors: Maud Mielvaque and Maximilien Rouer, C3D and adaptation/s
publications.desc: The report highlights that nature regeneration is a powerful lever for mitigating negative environmental impacts and for resilient adaptation of businesses, by securing supplies and reducing risks.

publications.title: La France Bleu Blanc Vert
publications.desc: One of the few books in French about adaptation of territories to climate change, with an original angle: how to protect human, urban and agricultural activities? Backed by 20 interviews of experts and companies, several 'umbrella' solutions — already existing, robust and proven — are presented to adapt France to climate change by 2050: agrivoltaic canopies, hill reservoirs, agroforestry for rural areas; photovoltaic canopies, cool roofing, plant canopies for cities.

publications.title: Les agriculteurs à la reconquête du monde
publications.desc: The book advocates a "triple revolution of consciousness" for French agriculture: changing the relationship with the consumer by selling solutions rather than raw materials, transforming production conditions by adopting ecologically intensive agriculture, and rebalancing relations between farmers, processors and distributors.

publications.title: Vous êtes libres de changer le monde
publications.desc: A book that encourages readers to overcome their fears and conditioning to transform society. It offers a triple journey: through the testimonies of "world-changers", an exploration of the psychological mechanisms of action, and a personal journey structured around the four seasons of change (waking up, transgressing, enjoying, recruiting).

publications.title: Réparer la planète
publications.desc: This pioneering book lays the foundations of a so-called positive economy, because it repairs the environment. It illustrates with examples that every activity could store carbon, regenerate biodiversity, depollute air, water and soil, and produce resources.
